plan: [ This auction is strategically equivalent to an English/second-price auction: the highest sealed bid wins and pays the second-highest bid (the clock stops at the runner-up’s exit). With independent private values and no future rounds to influence, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Overbidding risks negative profit if I win above value; underbidding risks losing when winning would have been profitable. Therefore, I will set my sealed bid equal to my value, $34, ensuring I only win when profitable and pay roughly the second-highest bid. ]

[ This two-stage format (sealed bid as exit in an ascending clock) is strategically equivalent to a second-price auction: the highest bid wins and pays the second-highest bid. With independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Bidding your value maximizes expected profit and avoids overpaying; if you win, the price will not exceed the next-highest bid, which is less than or equal to your value. There’s only 1 round, so no learning adjustments are needed. I will bid exactly my value: 28.0. ]

[ This auction is effectively second-price: the sealed bid sets my auto-exit; the winner pays the second-highest bid (the clock price where the runner-up exits). With independent private values and risk neutrality, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value to maximize expected profit and avoid overpaying or missing profitable wins. There’s no exploitable history (single round), and values are redrawn independently. Therefore I will bid exactly my value, $14.0 (valid $0.1 increment), to maximize long-run profit. ]
